    Britt bill would launch national office to combat financial fraud

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (496 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that britt has made fighting elder financial abuse a priority.
    • Industry observers note that A bill introduced by Sen.
    • The draft bill would establish a National Office for Scam and Fraud Prevention in the White House that would coordinate federal, state and private sector efforts.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that britt has made fighting elder financial abuse a priority. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    Industry observers note that A bill introduced by Sen. Katie Britt on Wednesday aims to combat a rising diversity of financial fraud by unifying the U.S. effort to fight it.

    The draft bill would establish a National Office for Scam and Fraud Prevention in the White House that would coordinate federal, state and private sector efforts. It is aimed at ensuring that federal agencies, law enforcement, financial institutions, telecommunications and technology companies and other groups work together, according to an overview from Britt.

    The upcoming office would promote intelligence sharing across the public and private sectors, coordinate consumer education efforts and improve assistance for victims.

    Britt, R-Ala., said the effort is needed because fraudsters operate nimbly utilizing social media while taking advantage of fragmented or disorganized responses from individual companies and government agencies.

    According to recent reports, “This effort is about bringing everyone to the table and making sure our response keeps pace with the criminals who are exploiting new technologies and gaps between sectors,” she said in a statement. “When we work together to identify threats earlier and share information more effectively, we can better protect American families and businesses.”.

    The office would develop a “lexicon of fraud” so that terms for different kinds of scams are standardized between various federal law enforcement agencies to promote a “whole-of-government response,” a Britt aide remarked.

    The office also would work to broaden the approach to combating fraud beyond just having financial institutions reimburse victims. It would tap telecommunications and technology companies to address fraud at its source, such as rip-offs that start as text messages, social media posts or online advertisements.

    Britt has made fighting elder financial abuse a priority. She is the sponsor of a bill that would allow state, local and tribal law enforcement agencies to use federal grant funding to investigate financial fraud, particularly scams targeted at the elderly.

    The measure highlights the prevalence of "pig butchering," a common technique where a predator cultivates a personal relationship with a victim over many months to extract the most cash.

    The House passed its version of the bill in September with overwhelming bipartisan support. The House sponsor is Rep. Zach Nunn, R-Iowa.

    Industry observers note that senior financial abuse also was the focus of a bill the House passed in an overwhelming 414-2 vote in June. The legislation, sponsored by Rep. Ann Wagner, R-Mo., would codify Securities and Exchange Commission guidance that permits mutual funds and their agents to postpone the sale of securities if there is a reasonable belief that financial exploitation of someone who is elderly or disabled is occurring.

    It's not clear whether the Senate will take action on these bills or Britt's by the end of the year.

    “If it doesn’t get through in the lame duck, it will continue to be a priority in the 120th [Congress],” the Britt aide said.

    Yet another giant new cruise ship takes to the sea

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (903 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The cruise world welcomed another giant on Wednesday as MSC Cruises took delivery of one of its largest ships ever, the 216,638-ton MSC World Asia.
    • Built at the massive Chantiers de l'Atlantique shipyard in Saint-Nazaire, France, the 20-deck-high, Asia-themed vessel is the third in the line's new World Class series of ships — by far the biggest ships that MSC Cruises has ever built.
    • Perhaps more notably, it is the tenth largest cruise ship ever built by any line, smaller only than Royal Caribbean's three Icon Class ships and six Oasis Class ships.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The cruise world welcomed another giant on Wednesday as MSC Cruises took delivery of one of its largest ships ever, the 216,638-ton MSC World Asia.

    Built at the massive Chantiers de l'Atlantique shipyard in Saint-Nazaire, France, the 20-deck-high, Asia-themed vessel is the third in the line's new World Class series of ships — by far the biggest ships that MSC Cruises has ever built.

    Perhaps more notably, it is the tenth largest cruise ship ever built by any line, smaller only than Royal Caribbean's three Icon Class ships and six Oasis Class ships.

    "Our ambition is simple: To give every guest the best holiday ever," MSC Group executive chairman Pierfrancesco Vago noted Wednesday during a dockside ceremony at the Chantiers de l'Atlantique shipyard to mark the vessel's official handover to MSC Cruises.

    MSC Group is the parent company of MSC Cruises and sister brand Explora Journeys, a luxury line.

    "We invested in rethinking spaces, developing latest concepts and reshaping the experience," Vago added during remarks from a stage set up just in front of the MSC World Asia's bow.

    Vago noted that 60% of the spaces on MSC World Asia are either new or significantly redesigned as compared to the two World Class ships already sailing, MSC World Europa and MSC World America.

    Like those two vessels, MSC World Asia has nearly 2,600 rooms and is capable of holding a whopping 6,758 passengers with every berth filled — more than almost any other passenger vessel afloat.

    It also has similarly massive dimensions with a length of 1,093 feet — the equivalent of nearly four football fields stacked end-to-end — and a width of 154 feet.

    But many of its interior and exterior venues, including a sprawling decktop water park with multiple waterslides and a record-setting dry slide that drops 11 decks, are different from what you'll find on the earlier World Class ships in ways major and small.

    Related: The terrifying, record-breaking slide on MSC World Asia.

    Among the most significant changes is the addition of upcoming dining and food concepts, including MSC Cruises' first pan-Asian restaurant and a Venchi chocolate and gelato venue.

    Like the earlier World Class vessels, the ship also offers a sushi bar, teppanyaki restaurant, American-style steakhouse and a branch of the Italian chain Eataly (at the moment found only on MSC World America), among 20 dining options in all.

    In addition to the water park and dry slide, MSC World Asia's top decks offer multiple pool areas; a suspended-over-the-ocean swing ride called The Cliffhangar; and a ropes course.

    Recent findings suggest that notable interior features include a three-deck-high dining and entertainment zone called the World Galleria, which is covered by one of the largest LED-lit ceilings at sea. An outdoor extension of this area, called the World Promenade, features more dining and entertainment, plus a new suspended, illuminated Dragon sculpture — part of the ship's Asia theming.

    Related: MSC Cruises cabins and suites guide.

    The arrival of MSC World Asia marks the latest milestone in MSC Cruises' rapid expansion.

    With the addition of MSC World Asia, the brand now operates 24 ships, up from just 13 vessels as recently as 2017. It has nine more on order.

    In a recent development, the ships on the way include five more World Class vessels scheduled for delivery by 2031. Also coming is a fresh class of four somewhat smaller, 180,000-ton vessels that will be known as the Frontier Class.

    Wednesday's delivery ceremony included a ceremonial lowering of the Chantiers de l'Atlantique and French flags in front of attendees and the raising of the MSC Cruises flag as well as the flag of Malta, where the vessel is registered.

    MSC Group chief financial officer Alexa Aponte Vago, who is married to MSC Group executive chairman Pierfrancesco Vago, served as the traditional "godmother" for the event, which included the smashing of a bottle of Champagne against the ship's hull.

    Joining her husband on stage, Alexa Aponte Vago cut a ceremonial blue ribbon to release the bottle of Champagne against the side of the vessel right on the letter C in its name.

    While it included a bottle smash, Wednesday's event was not the vessel's official naming. That will take place Saturday in Le Havre, France, at a much larger event.

    MSC World Asia will then head to the Mediterranean, where it will begin its first cruises with paying passengers on Dec. 4 with a voyage out of Barcelona.

    The ship initially will operate seven-night Mediterranean voyages that include stops in France, Italy, Malta and Spain.

    It has been revealed that in November 2027, it will reposition to the Southern Caribbean for seven- to 14-night sailings. The itineraries will include stops in Saint Lucia, Grenada, St. Maarten, Antigua and Barbuda, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Dominica, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.

    Founded in 1861, the Chantiers d'Atlantique shipyard in St. Nazaire is one of the world's most famous shipyards, known for building many of the world's largest cruise ships as well as naval vessels and wind-powered commercial ships. Notable vessels built at the shipyard include the SS Normandie, SS France, Cunard's Queen Mary 2 and several of Royal Caribbean's Oasis Class ships.

    The shipyard has built 20 vessels for MSC Cruises over the past 25 years.

    It is located at the mouth of the Loire River on the West coast of France.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., flanked by House Minority Whip Katherine M.
    • House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries won a closed-door vote of the Democratic caucus Wednesday setting him up to be the nation’s first Black speaker of the House, a historic step that follows Democrats’ staggering election wins earlier this month.
    • Jeffries, who had called for a recorded vote of the more than 250-member caucus that will serve in the next Congress despite facing no confirmed opponent, won decisively, 251-11.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., flanked by House Minority Whip Katherine M. Clark, D-Mass., and House Democratic Caucus Chair Pete Aguilar, D-Calif., hold a press conference in the Capitol after the House Democratic leadership elections on Wednesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries won a closed-door vote of the Democratic caucus Wednesday setting him up to be the nation’s first Black speaker of the House, a historic step that follows Democrats’ staggering election wins earlier this month.

    Jeffries, who had called for a recorded vote of the more than 250-member caucus that will serve in the next Congress despite facing no confirmed opponent, won decisively, 251-11. The margin suggests Jeffries will easily surpass the necessary 218 votes he will need on the House floor when the full chamber votes in January.

    “It's a high honor and a distinct privilege to stand before the American people today as a Democratic nominee to be the next Speaker of the United States House of Representatives,” Jeffries remarked at a press conference following the election.

    While Jeffries celebrates his win, he has continued to put an emphasis on unity before he faces what has been deemed the toughest job in Washington. Democrats’ massive majority will give him some margin for maneuvering as he balances the priorities of a complex caucus ranging from moderates to progressives.

    It has been revealed that “Our job is to fight MAGA extremism, not each other,” Jeffries responded when asked about the 11 defections and what they mean for the next Congress. “Fight MAGA extremism, and to get massive things done for the American people, and that is what we are going to accomplish together, beginning on January 3rd.”.

    Seven of the 11 members who intended to vote against Jeffries released a statement saying that conversations with leadership are still “ongoing” and that there is “work to be done,” but noting there has been “meaningful progress.” The seven included Reps.- elect Darializa Avilia Chavelier, D-N.Y., Adam Hamawy, D-N.J., Frederick Haynes, D-Texas, Melat Kiros, D-Colo., Donovan McKinney, D-Mich., Chris Rabb, D-Pa., and Claire Valdez, D-N.Y.

    It has been revealed that “Whether on Medicare for All, stopping ICE terror, getting money out of politics, or ending the genocide in Gaza, our constituents sent us to Congress with a mandate on these issues,” they wrote. “We have worked to secure commitments from Leader Jeffries in good-faith conversations.”.

    Newly elected House Democrats will meet with former President Barack Obama Wednesday night, where party unity will also be a likely topic.

    Sources indicate that “This is the beginning of a latest bargain, a new politics where hard work is honored and where people's voice is paramount, and where we have more confidence in the future than nostalgia for the past,” House Minority Whip Katherine M. Clark, D-Mass., noted at the press conference.

    Industry observers note that rep. Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., who made history two decades ago as the nation’s first female speaker, arrived for the vote chanting “Hakeem Jeffries!”, reflecting party leaders’ desire to start the long morning of balloting on a positive note.

    Jeffries' nomination followed the election of current Democratic Caucus Vice Chairman Ted Lieu, D-Calif., to serve as the caucus chair in the next Congress. Separate votes followed Wednesday morning, keeping Jeffries' leadership team intact: Clark, as the fresh majority leader and Democratic Caucus Chairman Pete Aguilar, D-Calif., as majority whip.

    It has been revealed that at his news conference, Jeffries noted that Clark was also making history as the first woman ever to serve in the position. Aguilar will also be the first Latino to serve as majority whip.

    In a recent development, “We've been looking at people's talents, not a particular gender or race, and I think that's a good thing,” outgoing Rep. Steny H. Hoyer, D-Md., a former majority leader, told reporters ahead of the election.

    In a recent development, “I think Hakeem Jeffries is going to be a good speaker,” Hoyer continued. “He has the confidence of the caucus, and he has a good leadership team that is close knit and very organized.”.

    Jeffries expressed confidence in the weeks leading up to his securing the top Democratic spot in the House, brushing aside questions about incoming members who had remarked they remained “undecided” ahead of the election.

    In a recent development, pelosi was nominated for speaker by acclamation ahead of her first election to the position in 2007. But Jeffries’ allies portrayed his decision to move forward with a recorded vote as a show of strength after a group of incoming progressives had floated forcing a recorded vote in the internal leadership race.

    According to recent reports, the entire leadership team will be tested despite their numerical advantage over Republicans by the same internal tensions facing Senate Democrats, where current Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., is being challenged for leadership of the majority by Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md.

    Jeffries stated Tuesday that the approach to the caucus vote mirrored the caucus’ 2018 transition from minority to majority, giving members an opportunity to weigh in on who was best positioned to lead based on their “track record, experience and vision.”.

    Jeffries has already outlined some of his top priorities of his speakership such as a hefty healthcare agenda, immigration legislation, and a multitude of investigations into the Trump administration.

    He also signaled Wednesday another area where his party’s restive base is likely to close ranks: oversight.

    “House Democrats will hold the crooks accountable, not for partisan reasons, but for patriotic ones,” he noted at his news conference.

Just a short flight or boat ride away, the archipelago was somewhere I returned to often, and still do. Yet what continues to surprise me is how different one island can feel from the next. I've always thought it was a shame that so many visitors to the Bahamas never make it beyond Nassau or Freeport. Eleuthera has some of the prettiest beaches I've seen, the water around the Exumas is almost unbelievably clear, and the Abacos have small waterfront towns that are worth exploring. Each island has its own personality, and even after years of visiting, there are so many I still want to discover.

    Renting a home is one of my favorite ways to experience it all. Beautiful beachfront villas, colorful cottages, and contemporary homes with pools overlooking the sea are everywhere in the Bahamas. Having your own place makes it easy to settle in, explore a little, and enjoy the particular rhythm of whichever island you've chosen. After so many visits, I’m eager to step slightly off the typical tourist path (although the resorts and hotels here are also beautiful), and these Bahamas Airbnbs are a great way to do so. Read on for my most-recommended rentals in the Bahamas, from beachfront stays to island cottages.

    Number of guests: 2Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Pink-sand beach, heated pool, covered veranda.

    Industry observers note that for couples who prefer a little privacy, this one-bedroom bungalow occupies a lovely stretch of Eleuthera's Atlantic coastline. A covered veranda faces the sea, and a king-size bed and kitchenette provide the essentials for a comfortable stay. The property shares a heated swimming pool with a few other accommodations, but the real attraction is the beach itself. The bungalow feels pleasantly removed from everything, with little to interrupt the sound of the waves.

    Neighborhood: Governor's Harbour area, EleutheraThings to do nearby: Pink-sand beaches, Governor's Harbour, local snorkeling.

    Number of guests: 2Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Private waterfront deck, bedroom ocean views, optional private chef.

    Some of the best places to stay in the Bahamas are the ones that make you feel completely surrounded by water. At this intimate one-bedroom retreat on Exuma, enormous bedroom windows look directly toward the sea, and a private deck provides access to the water below. The interiors are understated, with a kitchenette designed for light meals rather than elaborate cooking. A private chef can be arranged for dinner for an added fee, or guests can venture into nearby George Town for a delicious meal at one of the waterfront restaurants.

    Location: Near George Town, ExumaThings to do nearby: George Town waterfront, snorkeling, Exuma boat excursions.

    Number of guests: 14Bed and bath: 5 bedrooms, 4 bathsWhy we love it: Private pool, beachfront location, kayaks and paddleboards.

    In a recent development, sea turtles frequently visit the shallow waters of Hoopers Bay, and guests at Blu Wakes have an excellent vantage point for spotting them. The five-bedroom villa—four kings and a room for kids with two queens and a bunk bed—opens onto a beautiful stretch of beach, with a private pool overlooking the water. Kayaks and paddleboards make it easy to explore the bay, while concierge services can arrange everything from a private chef to a day trip exploring the Exuma cays. With room for 14, it's particularly well suited to extended families or substantial groups.

    Location: Hoopers Bay, Great ExumaThings to do nearby: Hoopers Bay sea turtles, George Town, Exuma cays excursions.

    Number of guests: 2Bed and bath: Studio, 1 bathWhy we love it: Beachfront location, porch, on-site beach bar.

    In a recent development, there's a clear appeal to a place like this where the biggest morning decision is whether to take your coffee on the porch or at the beach. This cheerful little cottage, called Tiny's Toes in the Sand, has rocking chairs overlooking Salt Pond Harbour, a kitchenette for simple meals, and a beach bar just steps away. At only 400 square feet, it's not a place for spreading out, but for two people looking to spend most of their time steps from the water, that's rather the point.

    Location: Salt Pond, Long IslandThings to do nearby: Salt Pond Harbour, Dean's Blue Hole, Cape Santa Maria Beach.

    Number of guests: 16Bed and bath: 7 bedrooms, 9 bathsWhy we love it: Infinity pool, outdoor kitchen, concierge services.

    Industry observers note that with seven bedrooms and more than 5,000 square feet of living space, Sea Salt Villa is designed for a crowd. The contemporary home sits within a gated community overlooking Emerald Bay, with expansive windows, an infinity pool, and a covered outdoor entertaining area. An outdoor kitchen makes casual dinners easy, while concierge services can help arrange private chefs and excursions. It's a particularly good option for extended families or groups of friends who want the space of a private home but still enjoy resort-style comforts. Plus, it’s located on a PGA golf course if you’re looking to get in a round or two, and guests can rent golf carts to drive around the community.

    There's a lovely sense of everyday island life at this two-bedroom apartment overlooking Anchor Bay. From the balcony, guests can watch boats coming and going, while the shared rooftop gallery is a particularly nice place to catch the sunset. The apartment has a well-equipped kitchen and two en suite bedrooms, and restaurants and shops are within walking distance. Beach chairs, towels, and a cooler are provided for exploring Eleuthera's coastline, making it easy to head out for the day.

    Location: Governor's Harbour, EleutheraThings to do nearby: French Leave Beach, Haynes Library, Governor's Harbour restaurants.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, do you love the great outdoors but still haven't found the right gear to make your adventures possible? REI has everything you need for whatever trip you're planning. Beloved by hikers, campers, and outdoor adventurers—myself included—REI has an excellent line of gear that spans everything from shoes and clothing to blankets to mountain bikes. Whether you’re a city-goer who just wants reliable outerwear and comfortable shoes to take on your next trip, or you’re a trekker who is preparing for a multi-day backpacking excursion, REI has all you’ll need to get started—and then some. Plus, there are some excellent deals you can take advantage of right now to make sure your budget won’t take a hit before you even set foot on your trip.

    Created in 1938, the brand is all about encouraging travelers’ love of the great outdoors—it was built on the founders’ dream of sharing their love of nature with the world around them—and in almost a century, REI hasn’t strayed from that ethos. Whether you’re a upcoming customer or a seasoned regular, there are plenty of ways to save on REI gear and clothing as long as you know where to look. And no matter where you're headed, travelers of all experience levels can find excellent gear, clothing, and travel accessories at an affordable rate. Read on to discover some of the best coupon codes and Black Friday savings at REI right now. Looking for more outdoor adventuring gear? Take a peek at our Snow Peak discount codes and Mountain Hardwear coupons.

    It has been revealed that black Friday is one of the best times of the year to shop thanks to the incredible savings at all your favorite stores. This year, REI is offering shoppers up to 50% off past-season styles from top brands like Arc'teryx, Cotopaxi, REI Co-op, Patagonia, and more. For the greatest bang for your buck, Head to REI’s deals section to browse through thousands of excellent savings on clothing, gear, shoes, and everything in between.

    Industry observers note that looking for a rain jacket or parka to protect you from the elements? Score savings on all you need to protect you against the elements. In need of some hiking boots for your next excursion? They’ve got you covered with hundreds of dollars in savings on all your desired footwear, including deals on favorites like 20% off men’s Bondi 9 Road-Running shoes and 50% off Merrell men’s Moab 2 Decon SE hiking shoes. You can also expect savings on backpacks (up to 60% off top brands like Osprey, The North Face, Patagonia, and more), as well as socks (10% off bundle deals when you buy three or more full-priced socks, and up to 70% off specific pairs).

    Buy more to save more with REI’s volume discounts this fall, which let you save up to 15% when you bundle multiple products—especially helpful when you’re purchasing significant-ticket items like a tent, bicycle, or kayak. A few of the products you can save big on are socks (take up to 10% off when you buy three or more full-priced pairs), cycle accessories (take up to 15% off bike accessories, clothing, and shoes when you purchase any full-price Co-op Cycles bike that same day), REI Co-op brand camping gear (save 10% on bundles of full price tents, sleeping bags, and sleeping pads, as well as 10% on backpacking food and snacks when you meet the minimum purchase requirement of 8 and 10 respectively), and finally 15% off full-price paddles when you purchase a kayak, canoe, or stand-up paddleboard.

    For more ways to save with REI, head straight to their discount page for the most up-to-date information on active REI coupons.

    Thinking of starting another hobby? There’s never been a better time to exercise your free will (and just plain exercise) by scooping up a new bike or tent to start your next outdoor adventure. Customers can expect savings of up to 30% off bikes and a whopping 50% off camping gear on REI’s deals page. Score massive on electric and mountain bikes, like 20% off the Co-op Cycles CTY 1.1 bike, so you’ll be able to traverse any terrain in style.

    For those interested in dipping their toe into the camping lifestyle, expect savings on plenty of the gear you’ll need to get started, including tents, sleeping bags, and camping essentials, like a whopping 50% off the REI Co-op Campwell 6 tent. Head out on your next significant trip through Yellowstone National Park or Glacier in style, and without the worry that you’ll be underprepared once you arrive. From camping chairs to keep you comfortable around the firepit to video cameras that always capture that perfect shot for your Instagram (or your memories), there are plenty of ways to save on all your necessities—and a few extras just in case.

    According to recent reports, no longer do you need to head to a store in person and battle it out for the last jacket on the rack: REI’s online outlet has tons of great gear to save on, all shoppable from the comfort of your own home. From shoes and socks to helmets, boots, and bags, expect huge savings on something for everyone. One of my favorites includes 27% off Smartwool Active Fleece Wind pants. There’s also plenty of other deals on travel gear worth calling out, like 30% off the CamelBak All Around travel tumbler and 41% off the Osprey Arcane small crossbody bag. On REI’s outlet page, shop top brands like Arc’teryx, Hoka, Keen, Osprey, Patagonia, Salomon, and Columbia, all in one spot.

    Sources indicate that members get more benefits, like free standard shipping on every order (5–7 business days)—a convenience that non-members can only reap the reward of when they hit the $60 minimum spend. Members also save 20% off on bike and snow shop services, have extended return windows of up to a year rather than the usual 90 days, get free ski and board wax and a flat tire tube with repair, and up to 33% off gear rentals. All of these benefits more than make up for the $30 fee.

    Recent findings suggest that give your gear and clothing a second life when you trade in gently used products to REI’s Re/Supply platform—and receive a gift card for eligible items. Simply fill out the trade-in form to get an estimate on your product’s eligibility and credit value. Then drop your products off at your nearest REI store. Once your trade-in is complete and your product has been evaluated, you’ll receive an email with an REI e-gift card that you’ll be able to use to purchase more of your favorite gear.

    According to recent reports, your used products will head to REI’s Re/Supply shop. Not only is this a great way to keep textiles and other items out of landfills, but you’ll get money back to spend on something else. These gently used secondhand products are shoppable as well, and at great discounts, so if you’re open to taking home a pre-loved item rather than springing for a new piece, expect to find some excellent savings. The brand is closing its online version of the shop, but customers can still purchase gently used items in its brick-and-mortar stores.

    One final way to keep to your budget and still get some great deals is by signing up for the REI credit card. Customers who open an REI Co-op Mastercard get a total of 15% in REI rewards (5% card rewards on all REI purchases and 10% Co-op member rewards). Cardholders also earn 1.5% in rewards on all other purchases when not shopping at REI. As a bonus, there is no annual fee, and the rewards no longer expire.

    REI credit cards are only available to members, so you’ll have to complete the one-time sign-up and $30 membership fee, but once you do so, you’ll be able to sign in online and validate your Co-op membership to join and start racking up rewards. All rewards are ready to be redeemed online and in stores at REI as soon as they pop up in your account. As a bonus, customers can expect a $100 REI gift card after their very first purchase outside of REI, but use it quickly, as the gift card expires 60 days after your account is opened.

    Dems express ‘points of anxiety’ over Trump’s summit with Putin and Xi

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1223 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, president Donald Trump prepares to shake hands with Russian President Vladimir Putin as China's President Xi Jinping looks on before the welcome banquet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday, Nov.
    • Some Senate Democrats have heartburn about President Donald Trump’s planned Thursday meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, but Republicans counter by saying he could get the Russian and Chinese leaders to budge on a list of challenges even as he appears politically weakened at home.
    • Sources indicate that trump arrived Wednesday in China’s Shenzhen economic zone on the banks of the Pearl River ahead of a high-level summit that was ostensibly slated to focus on paring each countries’ nuclear arsenal.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, president Donald Trump prepares to shake hands with Russian President Vladimir Putin as China's President Xi Jinping looks on before the welcome banquet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. (Iori Sagisawa / POOL / AFP via Getty Images).

    Some Senate Democrats have heartburn about President Donald Trump’s planned Thursday meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, but Republicans counter by saying he could get the Russian and Chinese leaders to budge on a list of challenges even as he appears politically weakened at home.

    Sources indicate that trump arrived Wednesday in China’s Shenzhen economic zone on the banks of the Pearl River ahead of a high-level summit that was ostensibly slated to focus on paring each countries’ nuclear arsenal. But before he left, Trump signaled the three-way talks also likely would include the artificial intelligence race, Moscow’s bloody war with Ukraine, global trade and his standoff with Iran.

    Industry observers note that the U.S. commander in chief’s tendency to sound deferential to Putin and habit of referring to Xi as a personal “friend” concerns many congressional Democrats. But Trump’s GOP allies on Capitol Hill, despite this month’s midterm election losses, still describe him as a dealmaker who has a chance to use his final years to bend Putin and Xi toward U.S. interests.

    Rick Scott, a Florida Republican who sits on the Senate Armed Services and Foreign Relations committees, said Tuesday he was hopeful that Trump could make some progress on at least one issue with the Russian and Chinese leaders.

    It has been revealed that “As we all know, China and Russia want to destroy our way of life,” he said. “But it would be great to reduce … nuclear stockpiles and make sure we're not going to ever get attacked.

    Still, Scott sounded skeptical about two world leaders Trump has tried to keep close during his two terms. “But do I trust Xi or Putin? No, they're a bunch of liars.” Asked if he worries Trump might trust them too much, Scott replied: “I don't think he trusts him any more than I do. … I'm glad the president's trying. Hope springs eternal. But do I actually really believe something good's going to come out of it? I don't.”.

    Outgoing House Armed Services Vice Chair Rob Wittman, R-Va., mentioned part of Trump’s talks on Thursday “should be to make sure the world is a safer place, to make sure we don't have aggressive behavior like Russia in an unprovoked attack against Ukraine.

    “They ought to be talking about how they don't do those sorts of things, how they don't threaten their neighbors, how they don't try to intimidate through the assertion of force that they ought to be able to work together to make sure we assure a safe globe,” noted Wittman, who lost his reelection race earlier this month.

    That comment came one day after Trump told reporters as he left the White House for Asia that he sees Putin “backing down a little bit” in his conduct of the war with Ukraine.

    It has been revealed that “I think he could be tougher. I think he could be a lot tougher, frankly,” Trump noted Monday. “I think he's backing down.”.

    Those kinds of deferential remarks about the Russian leader are a big reason why some Democrats have heartburn about Thursday’s meeting.

    It has been revealed that senate Armed Services member Mazie K. Hirono, D-Hawaii, noted Tuesday that she’s concerned about the Shenzhen summit because “I’m not sure what’s going to pop out of [Trump’s] mouth next — especially for a meeting with two guys he clearly likes.”.

    It has been revealed that sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., also a member of the Armed Services and Foreign Relations committees, mentioned he has “high hopes” for the trilateral meeting — but “maybe not high expectations.”.

    “I have some points of anxiety. I'm nervous about any discussion about Ukraine that doesn't involve the Ukrainians. And, so, some of the advance to this is like, ‘We're going to talk about ending the Ukraine war.’ You can't do that without Ukraine at the table,” Kaine said. “So the desire to bring about more peace and stability, that's a good thing to talk about. But no conditions about Ukraine and ending that war without them at the table? Not so sure about that.”.

    It has been revealed that during remarks Tuesday on the Senate floor, Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer criticized what he described as Trump’s misplaced priorities.

    “Enforcement of the newly introduced rules restricting China’s access to our most sensitive AI chips should start today,” the New York Democrat said, adding that Trump should focus more of his Asia swing on securing commitments from U.S. allies to block China from gaining an upper hand in the AI technology race.

    Trump touted just that on Tuesday during remarks in Manila at a U.S.-Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in the Philippines.

    “Since I returned to office, we've made major trade deals with Malaysia, Cambodia, Indonesia, as well as Japan, South Korea, and almost everybody, frankly, at the table,” he said. “And we've made many other vital agreements across the region spanning energy, critical minerals and technology.”.

    But on Wednesday, Trump appeared to have pivoted to the trip’s main event.

    He stood beside Xi at an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen and smiled as Putin approached. Trump extended his hand and shook Putin’s as the Chinese leader looked on.

    Scott, a Trump ally in the Senate, said Tuesday he sees the president “trying to build relationships to try to make sure we don't end up at war [because] he doesn't like war.”.

    It has been revealed that trump signaled Monday that he might press Xi for details on an alleged Chinese spy who had an affair with Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, costing the AI mogul his job as the manufacturer’s president and CEO. He also stated he could bring up Nvidia’s sales of sophisticated microchips that many lawmakers — Republican and Democrat — want to ensure remain in the U.S. for domestic AI development.

    The administration’s response to the turmoil at Nvidia, with Trump even suggesting he'd support Huang returning as CEO, is a rare area where Republicans have expressed concern publicly. House Energy and Commerce Committee Chair Brett Guthrie, R-Kent., wrote to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Wednesday seeking information about “the implementation of federal laws governing technology exports, in particular the application of export controls relating to semiconductor chips, the effect of which has a broad impact on America’s race with China to artificial intelligence (AI) dominance and the ability of U.S. companies to set global technology standards.”.

    Heather Williams, director of the Project on Nuclear Complications at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, wrote this week that for the three leaders, the “path is fraught with challenges.”.

    In a recent development, “Putin could diplomatically outmaneuver the Trump administration and make any progress on nuclear issues dependent on undermining Western support to Ukraine,” she wrote in an analysis for the Washington, D.C.-based think tank. “Even the optics of Trump and Putin negotiating while the war continues and as Russia ramps up missile strikes on Ukrainian civilian targets could be interpreted as undermining U.S. values.”.
